description: We are university students joining NASA Space Apps 2026 to build the Lunar Landing Site Navigator: a web tool to compare Moon south pole landing sites and dates, showing Sun and Earth positions, sunset and Earthset times, and power and communication windows. Stretch goal: a terrain-aware horizon from lunar elevation data.
summary:
Lunar Landing Site Navigator is a local, browser-based tool for evaluating candidate landing sites near the Moon’s south pole. It combines NASA’s 20 m LOLA terrain with the DE421 ephemeris to answer two operational questions: when a site receives sunlight, and when it has a direct line to Earth.
A ray-cast horizon accounts for real terrain and lunar curvature, so low ridges correctly block the Sun and Earth. Users can select a Product 78 region, click the map, or type coordinates, then adjust the date, mission duration, mast height and horizon range. The timeline plots Sun and Earth elevation against the terrain horizon and reports sunlit and Earth-visible percentages, the longest sunlit run, and the next sunset or Earthset.
details:
Lunar Landing Site Navigator is a local, browser-based tool for evaluating candidate landing sites near the Moon’s south pole. It combines NASA’s 20 m LOLA terrain with the DE421 ephemeris to answer two operational questions: when a site receives sunlight, and when it has a direct line to Earth.

A ray-cast horizon accounts for real terrain and lunar curvature, so low ridges correctly block the Sun and Earth. Users can select a Product 78 region, click the map, or type coordinates, then adjust the date, mission duration, mast height and horizon range. The timeline plots Sun and Earth elevation against the terrain horizon and reports sunlit and Earth-visible percentages, the longest sunlit run, and the next sunset or Earthset. Up to six scenarios can be saved and compared side by side. A 3D globe and whole-Moon view provide context, while an in-app guide explains every panel for non-specialists. Everything runs offline from the bundled DEM and NAIF kernels, with no API keys or external services.
